newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels give ultimatum to gold miners.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels give ultimatum to gold miners.

text.p: Rebels controlling a large area of eastern Zaire have ordered gold miners in their area to come forward and discuss the future of their mining concessions by January 3 or risk losing their assets.

Laurent Kabila, leader of the rebel group, told Reuters in Goma on Thursday: "We invite the companies to come and see us as soon as possible. If they don't come, the mines are our property and we will call in other investors to work them."
Official figures show that Zaire produced 33,365 troy ounces of gold last year -- but several times that figure was probably smuggled out of the country, diplomats say.
The Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) led by Kabila see the region's rich mineral resources as a way of financing their bid to take control of the fragmenting central African state.
"We have special groups working at extracting gold in some river areas," Kabila said. "That is a way of getting our income." But he gave no indication of the quantities involved.

The rebels took over the Sominki mining headquarters at Kamituga, 100 km (60 miles) southwest of Bukavu, after occupying Bukavu last October. But they have not been able to exploit the mining concessions, which are owned by a Canadian mining consortium, Cluff Mining and Banro.
The latest target for the rebel offensive is the Okimo gold concession at Kilo-Moto, 60 km (40 miles) north of Bunia, west of Lake Albert.
On Wednesday the rebels announced they had captured Bunia, but their claim has not been independently confirmed.
"We have not yet captured Kilo-Moto but it is the main target and we will soon take it," Kabila said.
